scenes.line1: Could you write a safe Bash script?
scenes.say: Ever freeze up when asked to write a Bash script live? Let's lock down the essentials so you don't.

scenes.label: Shebang
scenes.sub: Always start with a shebang and safe mode.
scenes.say: Start every script with a shebang and safe mode. This tells the system to use Bash and stops your script if anything goes wrong.

scenes.title: Quoting matters
scenes.say: Always quote your variables. Unquoted variables are the number one source of bugs, especially with spaces or empty values.
Use conditionals for decisions, loops to repeat tasks, functions for reusable code, and always check exit codes to handle errors.

scenes.question: What breaks most Bash scripts?
scenes.right: Forgetting to quote variables causes scripts to fail on spaces or empty values. Always quote them.
scenes.say: Interviewers see unquoted variables as a red flag. Always quote them, or risk breaking your script in weird ways.
